newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japan cement maker returns to the black.
newsitem.headline: Big Japan cement maker returns to the black.

text.p: Japan's second-biggest cement maker, Sumitomo Osaka Cement Co Ltd, said on Tuesday that it had returned to the black in the first half of the current business year due to aggressive restructuring.
Sumitomo Osaka said it expects the solid recovery to continue throughout the business year to March 31 and its 1996/97 parent current profit to be more than nine times as large as last year.

"As a result of restructuring measures, including closing our Hikone plant last year and reducing the number of employees, we posted an interim parent current profit of 1.15 billion yen ($10.3 million)," it said in a statement.
Its half-year period was to September 30. Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

Sumitomo Osaka posted a current loss of 303 million yen ($2.72 million) in the same period a year ago. It expects a full-year parent current profit of 5.0 billion yen ($45.0 million), up from 543 million yen ($4.89 million) in 1995/96.

Earlier this month, top cement maker Chichibu Onoda Cement Corp raised its forecast for its half-year current profit to 2.4 billion yen ($21.6 million) from its previous forecast of 1.0 billion yen ($9.0 million). Its actual half-year profit totalled 240 million yen ($2.16 million) a year earlier.
The company's restructuring efforts were behind raising of the forecast, it said. It will announce its half-year earnings later this month.
Sumitomo Osaka said that despite the current profit increase, the business environment remained tough for the Japanese cement industry.

Although domestic demand for cement rose 3.9 percent year-on-year, helped by public works projects planned to boost the overall Japanese economy, a fall in demand from other countries such as Taiwan pushed down exports by 14.6 percent from the year-ago period, it said.
As a result, Japanese cement makers' total cement sales in the six-month period increased only one percent from the same period a year ago to 45.69 million tonnes, it said.
Cement prices have fallen to low levels as a result of years of competition among cement makers for market share.
Cement makers have been struggling through various restructuring steps, aiming to recover from the slump. ($1=111 yen)
